problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-1,3⟩$, $c=⟨-2,4,-3⟩$, and  $u=⟨3,-7,3⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$

feedback.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,2,3⟩$, $c=⟨3,-7,-9⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,-3,-6⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
feedback.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ 2s-7t=-3 \\ 3s-9t=-6\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -7 & -3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ -t=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-t=1\,⟹\,t=-1.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+3t & =2 \\ -s+3(-1) & =2 \\ -s & =5 \\ s & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-5,\,t=-1,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-5b-c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-5)\cdot (-1)=5.$
